Feluda.description: A private detective known for his sharp intellect and investigative skills, he is the protagonist of the series.

Sushant Som.description: A secretary and associate of Mr Mallik who acts as a liaison and helper to Feluda's group during their travels.

Siddheshwar Mallik.description: Siddheshwar Mallik is a retired judge troubled by his past judgments, staying on a houseboat with his family, doctor, and attendants.

Calcutta.description: The former name of Kolkata, a major city in eastern India and the home of Feluda and his companions.

Himalayas.description: A vast mountain range in Asia, home to some of the world's highest peaks, including the region of Kashmir.

Vindhyachal.description: A range of hills in central India, considered less impressive than the Himalayas by the characters.

Western Ghats.description: A mountain range running parallel to the western coast of India.

Kashmir.description: A region in the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, renowned for its natural beauty and referred to as 'paradise on earth.'

Delhi.description: The capital city of India, serving as a transit point in the journey.

Srinagar.description: The largest city and summer capital of Jammu and Kashmir, famous for its houseboats and Dal Lake.

Pahalgam.description: A scenic town in Kashmir, known for its natural beauty and as a tourist destination.

Gulmarg.description: A hill station in Kashmir, popular for its meadows and as a ski resort.

Khilanmarg.description: A small valley near Gulmarg, known for its panoramic views.

Nanga Parvat.description: A prominent Himalayan peak, also known as Nanga Parbat, one of the highest mountains in the world.

Dal Lake.description: A famous lake in Srinagar, known for its houseboats and scenic beauty.

Mughal gardens.description: Historic gardens in Srinagar, built during the Mughal era, renowned for their design and beauty.

Jhelum.description: A river flowing through Srinagar and the Kashmir valley.

Durga Puja.description: A major Hindu festival, especially celebrated in Bengal, marking the worship of the goddess Durga.

Bengal.description: A region in eastern India, home to the Bengali language and culture, and the origin of Feluda and his companions.

chana.description: Roasted or fried chickpeas, a popular Indian snack.

houseboat.description: A boat designed or modified to be used primarily as a home, especially common on Dal Lake in Srinagar.

baujras.description: Traditional pleasure boats once used by zamindars (landlords) in Bengal.

zamindars.description: Landowners, often hereditary, who historically held large estates and collected taxes in India.

bearer.description: A personal attendant or servant, commonly employed by affluent families in India.

Mahmudia.description: One of the bearers on the houseboat, responsible for looking after the guests.

Abdullah.description: Another bearer on the houseboat, assisting with guest needs.

Harinath Majumdar.description: Mr Mallik's doctor and a medium who conducts seances to communicate with spirits.

Prayag.description: The bearer attending to Mr Mallik's group, later revealed to have a personal connection to a past case.

Sarkar.description: A businessman and gambler from Calcutta who assists in the search for Vijay Mallik.

Darjeeling.description: A hill station in West Bengal, known for its tea gardens and scenic beauty.

Simla.description: A hill station in Himachal Pradesh, also known as Shimla, popular for its colonial architecture.

Kathmandu.description: The capital city of Nepal, known for its temples and rich history.

Boulevard.description: A prominent road running along the southern edge of Dal Lake in Srinagar.

Venice.description: An Italian city known for its canals and gondolas, used here for comparison.

Shankaracharya.description: A temple atop a hill in Srinagar, dedicated to the philosopher Adi Shankaracharya.

Emperor Ashok.description: A Mauryan emperor of ancient India, referenced as the builder's father of the Shankaracharya temple.

Nishad Bagh.description: Nishat Bagh, sometimes spelled Nishad Bagh, is one of the Mughal gardens in Srinagar, renowned for its design and beauty.

Shalimar.description: Another famous Mughal garden in Srinagar, also called Shalimar Bagh.

Chashma Shahi.description: A Mughal garden in Srinagar, noted for its natural spring.

Char Chinar.description: An island in Dal Lake, named for the four chinar trees at its corners.

shikara.description: A small wooden boat found on Dal Lake, used for transport and sightseeing.

bungalow.description: A single-storied house, often with a veranda, typical in South Asia.

ghazal.description: A form of Urdu poetry, often set to music and expressing themes of love or loss.

sahib.description: A respectful term of address for a man, used in South Asia.

seance.description: A seance is a meeting at which people attempt to make contact with the spirits of the dead, often with the help of a medium; seances refers to such gatherings in general.

Ramswarup Raaut.description: A Bihari boy who was hanged for murder ten years ago and is contacted during the seance.

Mahatta & Co..description: A well-known photography studio and photo processing company in Srinagar.

spiritualism.description: A belief system or practice centered on the idea that it is possible to communicate with spirits of the dead, especially through mediums.

medium.description: A person believed to have the ability to communicate with spirits of the dead.

Tangmarg.description: A town near Gulmarg, serving as a gateway to the hill station.

Rajasthan.description: A state in northwestern India, known for its deserts and camels.

Bhopal.description: A city in central India, mentioned as the residence of Vijay's sister.

India.description: The country where the story is set.

Babu.description: A respectful term used in India to address men, often appended to names.

Vijay Mallik.description: Vijay Mallik is Mr Mallik’s son, sharing a houseboat with Mr Som, and is found unconscious on the mountain path after a mysterious incident.

Scottish Church.description: Refers to Scottish Church College, a prestigious educational institution in Kolkata.

Uttar Pradesh.description: A large state in northern India, where Vijay traveled after leaving home.

Kanpur.description: A major city in Uttar Pradesh, where Vijay met the sadhu Anandaswamy.

Anandaswamy.description: A sadhu (holy man) in Kanpur who helped Vijay overcome his drug addiction.

Maqbool.description: The previous bearer of Mr Mallik, who died suddenly and was replaced by Prayag.

sadhu.description: A Hindu holy man or ascetic, often regarded as spiritually advanced.

Sapru.description: A Kashmiri man who was sentenced to death by Mr Mallik and appears during a seance.

Shasmal.description: A spirit who appeared in an earlier seance and admitted to being a murderer.

Haridas Bhagat.description: The real murderer in Sapru's case, as revealed during the seance.

Manasbal Lake.description: A clear, scenic lake near Srinagar, famous for its underwater vegetation.

Punjabis.description: People from the Punjab region of India, often recognized by their distinct culture.

Kashmiri.description: Refers to people or things from Kashmir, a region in northern India.

Lidar.description: A river flowing through Pahalgam, popular for trout fishing.

Hollywood.description: The American film industry, referenced here for its depiction of Westerns.

Chandanwadi.description: A location near Pahalgam, known for its snow-covered bridge.

1978.description: A year referenced as the time since which Mr Mallik has felt remorse.

Ji, huzoor.description: A polite Hindi/Urdu phrase meaning 'Yes, sir' or 'At your service'.

Inspector Singh.description: The police officer in charge of the murder investigation.

Inspector Vajpayee.description: A police officer who previously worked with Feluda on a case in Rajgarh.

Rajgarh.description: A place referenced as the location of a previous murder case solved by Feluda.

Gujarati.description: Refers to someone or something from Gujarat, a state in western India.

Lalmohan Ganguli.description: A writer of thrillers and a close companion of Feluda, often providing comic relief and assistance during investigations.

Tapesh.description: Feluda's cousin and assistant who narrates the stories and helps in investigations.

Mr Jacob.description: Prayag's previous employer who lived on Park Street and left for England.

Park Street.description: A well-known street in Kolkata (Calcutta), famous for its restaurants and colonial-era buildings.

England.description: A country in the United Kingdom, referenced as the destination of Mr Jacob.

Chatterjee & Co..description: A company involved in import and export, where Vijay Mallik works.

Universal Insurance.description: An insurance company in Calcutta where Mr Sarkar works.

Pollock Street.description: A street in Calcutta, location of the Universal Insurance office.

The Calcutta Hotel.description: A hotel in Calcutta where Mr Sarkar's father worked.

Shikargah Lake.description: A specific lake mentioned as a local sightseeing spot, likely located near Srinagar.

Shiv temple.description: A Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, an important deity in Hinduism.

jeep.description: A type of vehicle commonly used by police and officials in India, known for its ruggedness and utility.

Indian Airlines.description: A major Indian airline that operated domestic and international flights, referenced for passenger verification.
